attributes.body:
When the adverbial particle でも is used more than once in a sequence, it is an extension of one of its regular meanings, analogical reasoning. However, several 'analogies' are being presented.

This use of でも is regularly translated as 'whether it is (A), or (B)', or 'neither (A) nor (B)', depending on whether the rest of the phrase is positive, or negative.

Literally, the translation of 〜でも〜でも is closer to the following:

Even if it's (A), even if it's (B), (C) is the result. (In a positive sentence)

Even if it's (A), even if it's (B), (C) is not the result. (In a negative sentence)

〜でも〜でも and にしても～にしても both show multiple options and that the result doesn't change. にしても～にしても has a slightly more hypothetical tone and works with verbs as well as nouns, e.g. 犬にしても猫にしても大変だ ('Whether it's a dog or cat, it's tough.').

かどうか expresses uncertainty, as in 来るかどうか分からない ('I don't know whether or not they'll come.'). 〜でも〜でも lists multiple alternatives and suggests the outcome is unchanged. For example, 雨でも晴れでも行く ('Whether it rains or shines, I'll go.').

〜でも〜でも and ～ても～なくても both express 'whether or not'. 〜でも〜でも shows multiple possibilities, e.g. クッキーでもケーキでも甘いものは食べたい ('I want sweets, whether it's cookies or cake.'). ～ても～なくても shows opposition, e.g. 行っても行かなくても大丈夫 ('It's okay whether you go or not.').

〜でも〜でも and にしろ～にしろ both express 'whether it's (A) or (B)'. にしろ～にしろ sounds a bit more formal and hypothetical and works with a wider range of grammar, including verbs. Both forms show that the result or evaluation doesn't change regardless of the options given.
